body:
## Observed failure

The #88 installed-package run on candidate `b6490f2` used a fully indexed 10,000-note vault and warm `embeddinggemma`. Five Windows exact-scan samples were 1955, 1577, 1606, 1214, and 75 ms (nearest-rank p95 1955 ms; budget ≤250 ms). Fedora scans were 61–76 ms. Cold page cache, concurrent I/O, and Windows scanning remain hypotheses; no cause was established.

## Final gate result and disposition

Installed candidate `095e765` passed the same five-query protocol on Windows: exact scans were 75.7, 76.1, 74.4, 74.0, and 73.2 ms (p95 76.1 ms). All five returned 20 results. Fedora also passed with p95 87.8 ms after its index reached 10,000 notes and zero waiting. Startup and graph repairs did not modify the semantic search implementation. Raw samples are in `docs/reports/evidence/88-perf-2026-09-27/` and the active verification matrix.

P2, deferred and non-blocking for external alpha. Owner: zulucode-design. Target: v1 feature-complete beta. Keep this issue open because the earlier Windows spike has no confirmed cause. Reclassify before alpha if it recurs or settled retrieval exceeds its budget.

## Follow-up work

- Reproduce the slow first scans on an installed Windows package while recording disk, SQLite, and CPU time; distinguish cold-cache cost from lock contention or external scanning.
- Fix the measured cause at the semantic-index layer if a reproducible cause is found. Keep exact ranking, category filtering, durable indexing, and stale-content checks.
- Rerun five indexed-vault queries on both supported machines. Local exact-scan p95 must be ≤250 ms without excluding slow samples.

Related: #88 and #158.

comments.body: Follow-up diagnosis: a read-only SQLite probe on the Windows fixture found 10,000 indexed notes, zero pending, and 10,024 embedding rows. Reading the embedding blobs took 458 ms on the first pass and 58/57 ms on repeated passes. A diagnostic no-bundle app build split the five settled searches: exact scans took 68, 87, 84, 69, and 111 ms; waiting for the semantic-index mutex was under 1 ms each time. This run does not reproduce the earlier 1214–1955 ms scans. Cold file-cache and/or transient machine I/O remain plausible; lock contention was not observed. Keep the original failed installed-package samples and rerun the exact protocol on the next installed candidate before changing the index architecture.

Recurred on installed candidate `1f01bf1` (perf row, 2026-10-01). Windows exact scans were 1131, 64, 66, 66 and 67 ms; the first query came 0.99 s after startup. Fedora's first scan was 95 ms, and the rest 59–63 ms.

Likely cause: #196. Each launch and exit rewrote the restored 5,000-word note without any edit, so every new app session started by re-embedding it. In this run the search session followed a graph session that did exactly that, so the first query's scan, whose timer includes taking the index lock, overlapped that indexing work. The final databases on both machines held one pending long-note revision.

#196 is being fixed now. The perf row then reruns on the new candidate, with the index checked as settled before each search session. If the first-scan spike remains without any pending work, this issue becomes a blocker and gets its own fix.
